Four AI workflows

Four AI workflows.

Qwen text and vision models work with the loaded map. Each workflow returns structured results.

01 · Preferences

Understand the traveller.

Voice or text becomes mobility settings: stair access, lift requirements, shelter preference and instruction format. The user reviews the settings before applying them.

Language → preferences → route planning
02 · Obstacle reporting

Locate the affected facility.

Vision extracts the visible barrier and signage. Map retrieval selects nearby facilities or paths. A confirmed match creates a timed event for rerouting.

Photo → facility match → event overlay
03 · Visual localisation

Match what the camera sees.

The system reads names, floor signs and visible objects, then compares them with nearby map records. A confirmed candidate becomes the new route origin.

Photo → map candidates → current position
04 · Cantonese guidance

Explain the current step.

Confirmed route facts provide the distance, floor, facility and action. The guidance workflow turns those facts into a short Cantonese instruction for browser speech.

Route facts → Cantonese text → playback
Photo matching

Photo-to-map
matching.

Separating image observation from map matching keeps every candidate tied to an existing node or facility.

Read the image

The vision role extracts text, floor labels, landmarks and obstacle evidence.

Retrieve map candidates

Floor and position narrow the search. Name and OCR similarity rank nearby records.

Compare the evidence

The matching role checks the observation against the retrieved records. Scores combine identity, evidence, proximity and route context.

Confirm and apply

The user confirms the candidate. The server validates its map ID and current journey context before updating the remaining route.

Routing and state

Session coordination.

The phone and control console use the same server session.

Constraints before preferences

Mobility policies remove unavailable edges. The planner then evaluates distance, exposure, effort or time. Sheltered and indoor objectives compare exposure before secondary cost.

Events over a stable graph

Facility closures and path reports form an event overlay. The base graph stays unchanged, and event validity determines which restrictions apply.

Shared phone and console

HTTP commands update the journey. Server-sent events deliver versioned state snapshots to both screens, including after reconnection.

Current-position rerouting

Completed steps remain in the journey. Confirmed location changes and active events replace the remaining route from the current anchor.
